newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 lower Monday, in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were mainly weaker early Monday, with dealers focused on AAs and crosses ahead of July's first tender day on Tuesday. September was down four stg at the midday break, to 1,140 stg.

Friday, New York cocoa futures ended lower in thin dealings. September settled down $10 at $1,680 a tonne after ranging between $1,694 and $1,676. Spot July lost $12 to $1,648, while the back months shed $11 to $13.
On the charts, traders pegged near-term support for the September contract at $1,670, followed by $1,655. On the upside, near-term resistance was seen at $1,696, and then Thursday's high of $1,722.

After the close on Friday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture its bulletin Tropical Products: World Markets & Trade left its estimate for the 1996/97 Ivory Coast cocoa crop unchanged at 1.10 million tonnes but shaved its forecast for Ghana's crop by 40,000 tonnes to 350,000 tonnes.
USDA said the attache in Abidjan had upwardly revised the Ivorian main crop estimate to 950,000 tonnes from 900,000 tonnes and lowered the mid-crop estimate to 150,000 tonnes from 200,000 tonnes.

It said the main crop was revised based on actual cocoa deliveries to processors, while the mid-crop estimate was lowered due to dry weather in February that adversely affected crop flowering and development in most producing areas.
